subtasks.title: Implement shared helper: OR-check for tokens:write or tokens:manage
details: Add a private helper function requireTokensWriteOrManage(c echo.Context) error in internal/handlers/pat.go
Call RequirePermission for 'tokens:write'; if it returns nil, return nil
Otherwise call RequirePermission for 'tokens:manage'; if it returns nil, return nil
If both fail, return HTTP 403 with message 'insufficient permissions'
API keys and admin tokens bypass this check via the existing RequirePermission behavior

subtasks.title: Implement shared helper: token lookup with user isolation and guard checks
details: Add a private helper lookupAndGuardPAT(ctx context.Context, tokenID, userID string, db *db.DB) (*PAT, error) in internal/handlers/pat.go
Query pats table WHERE id = tokenID AND user_id = userID; return HTTP 404 'token not found' if missing
Check revoked_at: if non-NULL, return HTTP 400 'token is revoked'
Check expires_at: if non-NULL and before time.Now().UTC(), return HTTP 400 'token is expired'
Return the PAT record for further processing by the caller

subtasks.title: Implement shared helper: permission format and registry validation
details: Add a private helper validatePermissions(perms []string, registry PermissionRegistry, ignoreUnknown bool) error
For each permission string, check it contains exactly one colon; if not, return HTTP 400 'invalid permission format: <permission>'
If ignoreUnknown is false (replace/add), check registry; if not found, return HTTP 400 'unknown permission: <permission>'
If ignoreUnknown is true (remove), skip registry check but still apply format validation
Return nil if all permissions pass validation

subtasks.title: Implement shared helper: privilege escalation check
details: Add a private helper checkPrivilegeEscalation(callerPerms, existingPerms, requestedPerms []string, authInfo AuthInfo) error
If caller is API key or admin token, return nil immediately
For each permission in requestedPerms, skip if already in existingPerms (keeping existing is always allowed)
For truly new permissions, check if present in callerPerms; if not, return HTTP 403 'cannot grant permission: <permission>'
Return nil if all new permissions pass the check

subtasks.title: Implement replacePATPermissions handler (PUT /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions)
details: Add func (h *PATHandler) replacePATPermissions(c echo.Context) error in internal/handlers/pat.go
Call requireTokensWriteOrManage; return on error
Parse token_id from path param; get userID via GetUserID(c)
Decode request body into UpdatePATPermissionsRequest; return HTTP 400 'invalid request body' on JSON error
If req.Permissions is nil, return HTTP 400 'permissions are required'
If req.Permissions is empty slice [], proceed to auto-revoke path (skip validation and escalation)
Otherwise: call validatePermissions(req.Permissions, registry, false); return on error
Call lookupAndGuardPAT to fetch current token; return on error
Call checkPrivilegeEscalation with caller perms, existing token perms, and requested perms; return on error
Within db.WithTx: UPDATE pats SET permissions=JSON(req.Permissions), revoked_at=NULL WHERE id=tokenID
If empty array: UPDATE pats SET permissions='[]', revoked_at=time.Now().UTC() WHERE id=tokenID
Return HTTP 200 with PATResponse including updated permissions and revoked_at if auto-revoked

subtasks.title: Implement addPATPermissions handler (PATCH /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions)
details: Add func (h *PATHandler) addPATPermissions(c echo.Context) error in internal/handlers/pat.go
Call requireTokensWriteOrManage; return on error
Parse token_id from path param; get userID via GetUserID(c)
Decode request body into UpdatePATPermissionsRequest; return HTTP 400 'invalid request body' on JSON error
If req.Permissions is nil or empty slice, return HTTP 400 'permissions are required'
Call validatePermissions(req.Permissions, registry, false); return on error
Call lookupAndGuardPAT to fetch current token; return on error
Call checkPrivilegeEscalation with caller perms, existing token perms, and requested perms; return on error
Compute merged set: start with existing permissions, append only permissions not already present
Within db.WithTx: UPDATE pats SET permissions=JSON(mergedPerms) WHERE id=tokenID
Return HTTP 200 with PATResponse showing merged permissions (revoked_at always NULL for add)

Decode request body into UpdatePATPermissionsRequest; return HTTP 400 'invalid request body' on JSON error
